findings.location: row weirdml::2: version, scoring.metric, scoring.notes, description vs c1 and SOURCE 1
findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 (retrieved 2026-11-28) is the current primary protocol and describes 'WeirdML v3' with '11 complex hand-made tasks', 15 configurations, and a scoring rule of '80% normalized area under its line on a logarithmic token axis, plus 20% of its final value'. The row claims version '2', '17 tasks', and metric 'Average Max Accuracy: per task, mean over runs of the maximum test accuracy across the 5 iterations per run'. The excerpt cannot establish continuity of the v2 identity against the current protocol, and the current page's task set, harness scope and scoring rule differ from the row's claims; SOURCE 3's scale summary settles nothing about metric meaning, computation, task set, harness or version.
findings.repair: Split the v2 observation from the v3 protocol: either retarget the row to the version the current page actually publishes (v3, with its 11-task, AUC-token scoring rule transcribed from SOURCE 1), or, if v2 is to be retained as a separate prior observation, bind it to the v2 page's own primary evidence (the 'WeirdML v2' link target is not captured in this packet) and re-verify its metric, task count and units against that page. Do not leave v2 fields asserted against a v3 protocol page.

findings.location: row weirdml::2: version_status and superseded_by vs c2 and SOURCE 1
findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 names 'WeirdML v2' under 'Previous versions' while serving v3 as the current release with a published release identifier ('WeirdML v3'). The row sets version_status 'published' (supported: the page publishes a release identifier, '2'), but sets superseded_by null while the protocol names a successor release (v3) of the same board. Per c2, a protocol that names a successor board contradicts superseded_by null. status 'active' is independently supported by SOURCE 2 (9 changed/added avg_acc values today), and the two fields are judged independently, so status itself need not flip here.
findings.repair: Set superseded_by to the registry id for the WeirdML v3 successor board (the protocol explicitly names it) or, if the v3 board is tracked as its own registry entry and this row's protocol passage is the v2 page rather than the v3 page, capture and cite the v2 page and re-judge supersession against that passage. Do not leave superseded_by null while the only captured protocol names v3 as the newer release.

uncertainties: I cannot recompute row or source hashes or execute transport/qualification checks; the owner-computed SHA-256s and the producer receipt are taken as given, per instructions.

SOURCE 1 is an excerpt of the v3 landing page; the 'WeirdML v2' link target is not captured, so whether a separate v2 protocol page would support the row's 17-task Average Max Accuracy description cannot be judged from this packet.
SOURCE 3's served values (1.729–93.573, 162 finite values) are consistent with the row's unit 'percent' and range [0,100]; no bounds mismatch is charged on that point.

status 'active' vs 'retained' for a superseded release is a judgment call c2 explicitly leaves open; I charged only superseded_by, not status, since SOURCE 2 shows the maintainer still serving values under this board's source field.
